UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user's profile information within the Polochka Exchange application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity.

username.description: A unique, user-chosen name for display purposes.

email.description: The user's email address, used for communication.

bio.description: An optional short description or biography provided by the user.

profilePictureUrl.description: An optional URL pointing to the user's profile picture.

locationName.description: A human-readable name for the user's primary location (e.g., city, neighborhood).

latitude.description: The geographic latitude of the user's primary location for proximity searches.

longitude.description: The geographic longitude of the user's primary location for proximity searches.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user profile was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating the last time the user profile was updated.

Category.title: Category
Category.description: Defines a classification for item listings, enabling organization and filtering.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Category entity.

description.description: An optional detailed description of the category.

imageUrl.description: An optional URL to an image or icon representing the category.

ItemListing.title: ItemListing
ItemListing.description: Represents an item that a user has listed for exchange on the Polochka Exchange platform.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ItemListing entity.

title.description: The main title or name of the item being listed.

description.description: A detailed description of the item, including its features and any notable conditions.

ownerId.description: Reference to UserProfile, indicating the user who listed this item. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N ItemListing)

categoryId.description: Reference to Category, classifying the item. (Relationship: Category 1:N ItemListing)

condition.description: The physical condition of the item (e.g., 'New', 'Used - Like New', 'Used - Good').

price.description: An optional suggested monetary value for the item, primarily for exchange context.

imageUrls.description: An array of URLs to images of the item, showcasing its appearance.

locationName.description: A human-readable name for the item's specific pickup or exchange location.

latitude.description: The geographic latitude of the item's location for proximity searches.

longitude.description: The geographic longitude of the item's location for proximity searches.

status.description: The current status of the item listing (e.g., 'available', 'pending exchange', 'exchanged', 'archived').

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the item listing was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating the last time the item listing was updated.

definition.description: Stores individual user profiles. The `userId` matches `request.auth.uid`. Some fields (`username`, `profilePictureUrl`, `locationName`, `latitude`, `longitude`) are publicly readable for item browsing and proximity searches, while others (`email`) are private to the owner.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier for the user profile, corresponding to Firebase Authentication's UID.

definition.description: Stores global, static categories for item classification. Read-only for all authenticated users; write access is restricted to administrators defined in `/roles_admin`.

params.name: categoryId
params.description: The unique identifier for the category.

definition.description: Stores all item listings. This collection leverages the `status` field for structural segregation of authorization; only items with `status: 'available'` are publicly browsable. Write/update access is strictly limited to the `ownerId` of the document, which must match `request.auth.uid`. Includes denormalized `ownerId` for authorization independence and simplified security rules.

params.name: itemListingId
params.description: The unique identifier for the item listing.

definition.description: A sentinel collection to store administrator UIDs. The mere existence of a document at `/roles_admin/{userId}` grants administrative privileges (e.g., to create/update categories) to the corresponding `userId`. This implements a Database Access Control (DBAC) model using 'Existence over Content'.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who has administrative privileges.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure for Polochka Exchange prioritizes secure, scalable, and debuggable authorization by strictly adhering to the core design principles. 

**Authorization Independence (CRITICAL):** This structure achieves authorization independence primarily through denormalization. Each `ItemListing` document explicitly contains an `ownerId` field, which directly corresponds to the `UserProfile` `id` of the listing creator. This allows Firestore security rules to verify ownership directly using `request.auth.uid == resource.data.ownerId` for read/write operations on listings, completely eliminating the need for expensive and complex `get()` calls to parent or related collections. Similarly, `UserProfile` documents are path-based (`/users/{userId}`), making `request.auth.uid == userId` the direct authorization check. For administrative roles, a dedicated `/roles_admin/{userId}` collection uses 'existence over content' for authorization, which is atomic and avoids `get()` calls for role checking.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):** The structure facilitates Query Access Patterns (QAPs) by using structural segregation and explicit state modeling. 
*   **Global Item Browsing:** All item listings are stored in a single top-level collection `/item_listings/{itemListingId}`. The crucial `status` field (e.g., 'available', 'draft', 'archived') in the `ItemListing` entity is used to manage security posture. When users browse public listings, they will issue queries explicitly filtering by status, e.g., `db.collection('item_listings').where('status', '==', 'available')`. Security rules then enforce that only documents matching `status == 'available'` are readable by non-owners, ensuring that rules do not implicitly filter query results, but rather validate explicit client requests. This makes the authorization intent clear and simplifies rule logic.
*   **User-Specific Item Management:** A user can retrieve all their own listings (regardless of status) by querying `db.collection('item_listings').where('ownerId', '==', request.auth.uid)`. Rules grant full read/write access to the owner based on the `ownerId` field.
*   **Category Listing:** Categories are stored in `/categories/{categoryId}`. As these are global and mostly static, rules allow read access to all authenticated users for browsing, and write access only to administrators.

**Structural Segregation and Access Modeling:**
*   **User Profiles (`/users/{userId}`):** Follows the 'Private Data' and 'Hierarchical Paths for User-Owned Data' principles. Each user's profile is directly accessible via their UID, making ownership explicit. Public fields (e.g., username, profile picture, location for proximity searches) can be read by others, while sensitive data (e.g., email) is restricted to the owner.
*   **Categories (`/categories/{categoryId}`):** Adheres to 'Structural Segregation' as a top-level collection for global, administrative data. Its uniform read-only security posture for most users simplifies rules.
*   **Item Listings (`/item_listings/{itemListingId}`):** While not a subcollection of `/users/{userId}`, it maintains strong ownership through `ownerId`. This top-level approach facilitates global browsing queries (e.g., location-aware search) without requiring complex fan-out queries across user subcollections. The `status` field provides internal 'Structural Segregation' by differentiating public from private/draft items.
*   **Admin Roles (`/roles_admin/{userId}`):** Implements 'Global Roles (DBAC)' via 'Existence over Content', providing a clear and efficient way to assign administrative privileges for tasks like category management without custom claims or complex data structures.
